lonely: WRITE FROM THE LONELY VIEWER'S SIDE
Before you write, picture one real person alone tonight. Write so that person feels seen in the first two seconds and is not alone by the last line.
depth: Mine John 13 for the details most people skip (who is where at the table, what Jesus knew, what He did with that knowledge, what the night means). Build the film on the richest detail you find.
hook: Most viewers decide in 2 seconds. Write the strongest honest hook you can and make every line pull to the next. The payoff must be worth the wait.
plain: Write so a viewer with school English and no Bible knowledge understands every line on first hearing, and a lifelong Bible reader still learns something.
judge: Write the best film you can. Use your own judgment on everything.
